scope: Research only: additional free/no-paid-login sources for movies, television, and real English anime dub. VIPTV migration remains paused. No new UI or provider integration in this task.

best_new_result.recommendation: First new all-in-one provider to prioritize for a strict native English implementation; MovieBox remains the independent-CDN backup. Sample stability is not uptime/SLA evidence.

cache.expiry_source: Expires query parameter of the actual signed HLS URL, approximately three hours after issuance in sampled Castle requests. It is an upper bound, not guaranteed availability.
cache.caveat: One label-only spaced selection missed Demon Slayer English; the exact already-returned file contained eng audio index 1 and was decoded after selecting it. Preserve the raw miss plus recovery rather than relabeling the phase perfect. Castle and Citadel both use img1.hscow.com/img1.fcxmb.com. These provide resolver alternatives, not independent CDN redundancy.

castle_api.transport: Native HTTP with AES-128-CBC encrypted JSON. The anonymous API returns its current security key; derive/decrypt in memory using the referenced implementation. No account cookie or Cloudflare solver was needed in these tests.
pitfalls: Do not drop English tracks merely because another track has existIndividualVideo=true.
For shared multi-audio files, a language label or languageId request does not force the player audio. Read actual HLS/muxed language metadata and choose English audio explicitly.
Language variants can share a media URL; URL deduplication must retain language/required-audio metadata.
Request the exact season movieId and episodeId. The reference JS matcher falls back to its first search row; a production adapter must reject unrelated titles/types/years instead.
Keep 16-digit catalog identifiers as strings: JSON floating-point rounding can corrupt them.
The research prototype corrects track filtering and inspects decoded media audio tags; it is not an SDK production adapter.

throughput_findings: MovieBox 30/30 short decodes do not imply smooth highest-quality playback. A 60-second default-quality Breaking Bad test timed out after 125 seconds at 57.493 seconds decoded. Inception/Frieren took about 96/101 seconds for 60 seconds of media.
Selecting the actual 480p representation passed 5/5 60-second clips in approximately 21–36 seconds. Players should adapt quality to measured throughput.
Castle passed all five 60-second clips in approximately 1–6 seconds wall time, with English audio selected. ffmpeg null output measures transfer/decode, not on-device rendering.

Do not classify them permanently dead. The first VM screen lacked AbortSignal; it was corrected and rerun, and a separate readable Castle adapter was required.

persistent_metadata: Strict TMDB/AniList/MAL to provider title/season/episode IDs, with source version and language variant identifiers. Retain until a mismatch/not-found triggers revalidation.
Verified English-track identity tied to the exact file/manifest version, not just the show or provider. Revalidate if the file changes.
Per-provider latency/success history, updated and aged over time.
Protocol/domain configuration version; refresh on service errors because hosts change.
cache_guidance.signed_media: Persist full playback URL, required request headers/cookies, exact media identity, required English audio selection and observed expiry together. Reuse until the earliest known expiry minus a safety margin, then refresh that exact media/provider entry. HTTP/network failure still needs bounded revalidation.
observed_not_guaranteed: MovieBox fixed original URLs passed at approximately 69 minutes.
Older Citadel signed URLs on Castle-shared CDN passed at approximately 60–80 minutes.
Castle signed URL Expires advertised approximately three hours. Actual playback at the full three-hour boundary has not been tested.
No permanent stream-URL validity, universal five-minute guarantee, next-episode prefetch, or persistent SDK cache was implemented.

method.short_pass: ffmpeg exit 0, >=24 frames, >=7.8 seconds decoded, nonzero decoded audio. English Castle results additionally select actual eng/en audio tags, followed by speech classification.
method.long_pass: ffmpeg exit 0, >=59.8 seconds decoded, nonzero decoded selected audio.
method.language: faster-whisper tiny CPU/int8, bounded 22-second dialogue clips. Anime and Breaking Bad at 480 seconds; Inception supplemented at 720 seconds due sparse earlier dialogue. Classification is automated, not a human listening claim.
limitations: Five selected popular titles, one connection, bounded clips and short repeat windows; no whole-catalog, full-episode, multi-day uptime or other-device verification.
Some independent research processes overlapped, so transfer timings include concurrent load and are not universal speed rankings.
SDK work remains unchanged by this research task. No production/API integration, deployment, UI or Cloudflare plugin added.
Context7 lookup returned unrelated tracking/TV services for Castle TV; protocol evidence comes from current primary extractor implementations and live calls.
